_meta._comment: Correlated/enriched alerts, 1-year retention via ISM (ism-alerts-365d.json attaches by index pattern, not by a template setting). v4: ai.engine/ai.model added so the dashboard can show which LLM actually produced a verdict (ollama vs stub), see services/ws5-ai/llm_adapter.py. v5 (gap-hunt finding, 2026-08-23): services/ws4-detection/main.py::make_alert() copies `src_endpoint`/`actor` WHOLESALE from the triggering event, which events-common.json maps far more richly (reputation, location, port, hostname, uid, domain) than this template did -- those real fields on real alerts landed in _source but were NOT indexed/searchable/aggregatable in alerts-*, silently, with no error (a dashboard filter on e.g. src_endpoint.location.country works against events-* and returns nothing against alerts-*). Expanded to match. Also dropped the dead `siem.*` block: make_alert() never sets a `siem` key on an alert doc at all (alerts carry `tenant_id`/`sector` as top-level fields instead, per router.py) -- those three properties could never be populated. v6 (gap-hunt finding, 2026-08-26): WS-5's classifier tier writes `classification.{category,priority,confidence}` onto the alert doc (services/ws5-ai/classifier.py); under dynamic:false those fields were unmapped -- stored but not searchable/aggregatable (a dashboard filter on classification.priority returned nothing). Mapped here. v7 (gap-hunt finding, 2026-08-27): dst_endpoint was not mapped at all even though make_alert() copies it and 6 shipped rules key on the destination (see main.py) -- under dynamic:false dest lookups on alerts-* came back empty. Mapped the ip/hostname/port the destination rules key on. v8 (review finding, 2026-08-27): make_alert() now sets `event_ids_omitted` (an integer count) instead of embedding a truncation marker string inside `event_ids` itself -- see engine.py's Rule.contributing_event_ids docstring. Only present when the _MAX_CONTRIBUTING_IDS cap actually bit.
